newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Philips to cut stake in ASML.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Philips to cut stake in ASML.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Thursday it would cut its minority stake in chip equipment maker ASM Lithography in a move which is set to raise some 400 million guilders ($217 million).
Separately ASM Lithography reported 1996 net earnings jumped 65.7 percent to 217.7 million guilders from 131.4 million.
"Philips intends to offer 3,950,000 ordinary shares...in an international offering," ASM Litho and Philips said in a joint statement accompanying ASML's results.
"Philips will use the proceeds of its offering for general corporate purposes. ASML will not receive any of the proceeds from the sale of the shares by Philips," the two companies said.
Philips currently owns a 35.4 percent stake in the manufacturer of wafer steppers for semiconductor production.
It will be left with a 23.9 percent stake in ASM Lithography after the secondary offering and has agreed to keep this holding until March 20, 2000.
The rise in ASM Lithography's 1996 earnings was at the lower end of analysts' forecasts of 210-241 million guilders.
ASM Lithography also announced plans for a two-for-one share split, saying it would seek shareholder approval for the move at its annual shareholders meeting on April 3, 1997.

The company, which has a dual listing on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange and U.S. Nasdaq, said that after last year's slowdown in the semiconductor industry the outlook for the first 1997 half was "moderate" but could pick up in the second.

"While we expect that the first half of 1997 will be consistent with the moderate forecast of the semiconductor equipment industry, we anticipate that demand for semiconductor equipment may strengthen in the second half," ASM Litho said.
It said 1996 profits per share grew 57 percent to 6.36 guilders from 4.06 guilders a year earlier.
Sales rose to 1.33 billion guilders from 920 million.
On the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, ASM Lithography shares opened a guilder lower on the news at 110.00, falling heavily to 104.00 in the first 90 minutes of trade.
